judged_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — P1 (93%): HubSpot likewise has no mapping from the documented sync response (`access token and expiry date`) to HubSpot's required `HubspotToken` fields: `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(`. The returned native `Response` is treated as a HubSpot SDK token and then `expiryDate`, `expiresIn`, and `accessToken` are read directly, so the credential-sync endpoint cannot provide a usable HubSpot refresh result.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts lines 176-193, the code wraps the HubSpot SDK call in refreshOAuthTokens(). The refreshOAuthTokens function (lines 3-21 in refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns either the result of the sync endpoint fetch (a Response object) or the result of refreshFunction(). When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, it returns a fetch Response, not a HubspotToken. The code then tries to use hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn, hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken etc. (lines after the shown diff), which would fail because a Response object doesn't have these properties. This is a real type mismatch bug when credential sync is enabled.
